hook_text: Forty degrees in the afternoon. A blanket needed at night. And almost no rain all year. Where is that?
clip_script: The Namib Desert in Namibia. Red dunes taller than a hundred-storey building. At midday the sand is too hot to walk on barefoot. At night, under a sky full of stars, the temperature drops sharply. Hot deserts lie near the tropics, on both sides of the equator, from the Sahara to the Kalahari. They get less than two hundred and fifty millimetres of rain a year. Clear skies let the heat in by day and out by night.
visual_style: Whiteboard world map with yellow desert patches along both tropics, then a climate graph with tiny rain bars, then a day-and-night split scene of a dune.
mood: Bright and dramatic, like an adventure under a blazing sun.
pacing: A slow sweep across the dunes, a clear map tour, then a step-by-step look at the climate graph.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find five hot deserts on a world map in your atlas.
